correctness.rationale: For common \(n\) and \(S\), Theil \(T\) ordering is exactly the ordering of \(Q=\prod_i x_i^{x_i}\), while mean-log-deviation ordering is the reverse ordering of \(P=\prod_i x_i\). The exhaustive partition census covers every admissible profile because positivity forces \(n\le S\). It finds no weak-order discrepancy for \(S\le10\) and exactly three strict reversals at \(S=11\).

value.rationale: \(GE(0)\) and \(GE(1)\) are canonical decomposable inequality measures chosen specifically for different lower-tail and upper-tail sensitivity. The result gives the exact smallest positive-integer resolution at which that distinction changes an ordinal comparison and classifies every reversal at the sharp layer.
